newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to change insurance tax scheme.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to change insurance tax scheme.

text.p: Philippine finance secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Friday he would ease the heavy tax burden imposed on life insurance policies.

At present, the government taxes the insurance premiums and receives a documentary stamp tax on the sum insured which "results in a significant amount of added cost in the overall pricing of life insurance products."
Life insurers in the country have one of the lowest penetration rates in the region.

"We shall look into this concern to see what appropriate measures can be adopted so that we can rectify whatever distortions there may exist under the present tax structure," De Ocampo told participants in the Life Insurance Summit.

"I would like to assure you that our policy is to ensure a simple but efficient tax system and, if and when it is necessary to rationalise the tax rates on insurance products, we will not hesitate to do so."
Aside from the tax structure, De Ocampo also promised to ease the licensing procedure by giving a continued validity of licences instead of the present one-year licence renewable every year.
"We have submitted a proposal to Congress in this regard and we hope to have this passed soon," he said.
